speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to help me understand your condition, have these symptoms been present for more than a few days, and did you have any close contact with someone who was recently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The combination of a 4-day incubation period after rhinorrhea and headache, followed by a rash that starts on the face and spreads to the trunk while sparing the perioral area, is classic for measles. I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation.
